sturmtiger.title: File:Sturmtiger ’19 red’ (s-n 205543) – Patriot Museum, Kubinka (38240137396).jpg
sturmtiger.artist: Alan Wilson from Stilton, Peterborough, Cambs, UK
sturmtiger.description:
German WW2 era Heavy Assault Gun
Official designation:- Sturmmörserwagen 606/4 mit 38 cm RW 61
Manufacturer:- Alkett
Built:- October 1943 to January 1945
Total Production:- 19
Main Armament:- 380mm RW61 rocket launcher L/5.4
The Sturmtiger (Assault Tiger) was based on the chassis of the Tiger I but fitted with a 380mm rocket launcher to support infantry fighting in urban areas. Despite the first prototype being presented to Hitler in October 1943, production was not requested until April 1944. The first three conversions, using rebuilt Tiger I chassis, were complete by August 1944 with the rest of the nineteen produced being finished by January 1945.
The type saw action during the Warsaw uprising and later during the battle for the bridge at Remagen, Germany.
Captured by Soviet forces in the Elbe area in April 1945, this late model Sturmtiger is one of only two survivors and has recently been repainted into an accurate colour scheme and markings. It is on display in Hall 11 of the Patriot Museum Complex.
Park Patriot, Kubinka, Moscow Oblast, Russia.

25th August 2017
sturmtiger.categories: Photographs by Alan Wilson|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Sturmtiger in the Patriot Museum Complex, Kubinka

flakpanzer.title: File:Flakpanzer Gepard (9394460358).jpg
flakpanzer.description:
The Flugabwehrkanonenpanzer Gepard ("anti-aircraft cannon tank Cheetah", better known as the Flakpanzer Gepard) is an autonomous, all-weather-capable German self-propelled anti-aircraft gun (SPAAG). It was developed in the 1960s and fielded in the 1970s, and has been upgraded several times with the latest electronics. It constituted a cornerstone of the air defence of the German Army (Bundeswehr) and a number of other NATO countries. In Germany, the Gepard was phased out in late 2010 to be replaced by "SysFla", a mobile and stationary air defence system using the LFK NG missile and the new MANTIS gun system. The mobile platform of SysFla will likely be based on the GTK Boxer.

Source : Wikipedia

raketenjagdpanzer.title: File:RakJgPz (SS11) PzJgKp 360 Külsheim, 1978.jpg
raketenjagdpanzer.description:
Raketenjagdpanzer 2 (RakJgPz 2, SS11), PzJgKp 360 Külsheim; photo in Külsheim (Main-Tauber-Kreis), Prinz-Eugen-Kaserne, 1978.
Formation of Panzerjägerkompanie 360 on Oct. 16, 1967 from the regular personnel of Ausbildungskompanie 10/12 Külsheim, and from the Panzerjägerzug of 5./PzGrenBtl 362 Walldürn.
Acquisition of the first Raketenjagdpanzer 2 in February/March 1968, retraining of the tank drivers from the RakJgPz 1 (on HS 30 infantry fighting vehicle chassis) to the Raketenjagdpanzer 2.
Depiction of the Prinz Eugen barracks area on the official 1:25,000 topographic map (Landesvermessungsamt/State Surveying Office Baden-Württemberg, published in 1997) on BayernAtlas.de: https://v.bayern.de/pxbCz.
